title: Olduvai Gorge: The Cradle of Mankind on Your Safari Route
excerpt: Olduvai Gorge, between Ngorongoro and the Serengeti, is one of the world's most important sites for human origins. Worth a stop on your route.
body:
Olduvai Gorge (more correctly spelled Oldupai) is a steep ravine in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Fossils and stone tools found here have helped scientists understand early human evolution.

## Why it is famous

From the 1930s onwards, Louis and Mary Leakey and other researchers found important fossils and stone tools here, including remains of early hominins. Nearby, at Laetoli, fossil footprints of early hominins were found, estimated at about 3.6 million years old.

## Visiting

There is a museum and a viewpoint over the gorge. A short talk by a guide explains the layers and the discoveries. A stop of about an hour is enough for most people.

## On your route

Olduvai lies on the road between the Ngorongoro Crater and the Serengeti, so it is easy to include.

## The name

The gorge is named after the Maasai word for the wild sisal plant that grows here.

## Combine

Add a visit to a Maasai village respectfully; see [visiting a Maasai village](/blog/visiting-maasai-respectfully/).
